title: Tests pin the relay v4 contract wiring
lead: Tests fail if `relay-run`'s `--json` contract string stops coming from `ai.contract_line()`, or if the orchestrator text drops its `--parent`, disputes or gate-resume rules; two docs lines say the orchestrator follows only the one-slice parts of `slicer ai relay`.
findings_note: s296 review 2026-10-16, Low: literal contract string and unpinned orchestrator bullets
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing the contract text itself, or inlining Gate, Every brief and Stop into the orchestrator text (an open owner question from s296).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The s296 review (2026-10-16, a Low finding the gate let through) found two gaps: a literal `"relay v4"` in the `cli.py` JSON instead of `ai.contract_line()` passes every test, and no test pins the orchestrator text's bullets for recording steps with `relay-run step --parent`, for disputes, or for resuming the reviewer as the gate. The next contract bump could leave the JSON behind, or a later edit could drop a rule, silently. The reviewer also noted that `docs/commands.md:19` and `CHANGELOG.md:11` say the orchestrator follows "never the outer session's steps". That is accurate for what it follows but not for what it reads, since it reads `slicer ai relay` for its one-slice parts.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `tests/test_ai.py`:
  - patch `ai.RELAY_CONTRACT` (or `contract_line`) and assert the `ai relay --json` and `ai relay-orchestrator --json` `contract` values follow it;
  - assert the orchestrator text names `--parent`, a disputes rule, and resuming the reviewer as the gate.
- `docs/commands.md:19` and the v1.12 CHANGELOG line: "follows only the one-slice parts of `slicer ai relay`".
- `src/slicer/cli.py` only if the JSON does not already call `ai.contract_line()`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; mutation-check each (a literal contract string in cli.py; delete each bullet in turn).
2. Fix the two docs lines.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
